::: {.callout-note}
**This page is for the facilitator.** It is left out of the navbar, so nothing on the site links to it. The track pages under `tracks/` are participant-facing and contain no instructor guidance, which is collected here and in the run sheets of the [facilitator guide of the case study](guide.qmd).
:::

## The formats

The facilitator chooses the format, and the link sent to the participants of a delivery leads to it, while the Formats section of the opening page is the way in to every format. Each track is an ordered route through pages of the site, with a docked sidebar of its own (`_sidebar.yml`) that lists its pages and the tools that it uses, an exercise page that sets out its tasks, and a slides page embedding the slides on which it runs. Each part page of a track carries the instructions for that part, with buttons into the page where the work is done, and the previous and next links at its foot follow the order of the sidebar. The timings are kept in the run sheets of the facilitator guide, and the participant pages give none, apart from the total of each stage of the self-taught format. Name the track of a delivery in `delivery.track` of `_variables.yml`, and the callout of the opening page links it; the navbar then shows a participant the last track page that they opened.

| Format | Track | Slides |
|---|---|---|
| Part-day format, browser only | `tracks/short/` | `live/short.qmd` |
| Full-day format | `tracks/day/` | `live/day.qmd` |
| Multi-day format | `tracks/long/` | the slide decks of day 1 on the AR4DS site, `live/day.qmd` on day 2, and the slide decks of day 3 |
| Self-taught format | `tracks/independent/` | `live/day.qmd` |

**What the full-day format holds.** The three one-day focuses of October 2026 (open science, data tools, methods) were merged into one workshop on 6 November 2026, in four parts: the claim and credibility, with SCORE in brief and its robustness study (Aczel et al. 2026); the estimand and the causal graph; the reproduction; and robustness, which holds the menu, the class chart with its submissions, the curve of the claim, the replication and the declared analysis. The tools are taught by the modules of the AR4DS site before the day, and live on the first day of the multi-day format. The participants in the full-day format do the tasks in the workspace, in their IDE, and the slides show each step with its output and stand in, with the browser lab, when an installation fails.

## The browser lab

The browser lab is a page that runs R in the tab of the browser and holds the six tasks of the exercise beside the workspace. It is live: it loads the data of the case study, about 100 KB of emails, and runs the code of the tasks on them, each fit in a fraction of a second. The web slides carry the same cells, with the same helpers, which are one file, `_includes/_lab-helpers.qmd`, beside the graph helpers of Task 2 in `_includes/_lab-graph.qmd`, and the lab is the fallback of both slide decks. The causal-graph task prints the answers that the pipeline computed with dagitty for the graphs that the cell offers, because dagitty cannot run in the tab; any other graph goes to the workspace.

## The slides {#the-decks}

The web slides used in the part-day format and the full-day format, `live/short.qmd` and `live/day.qmd`, are assembled from the segments of `live/_segments/`, of which those with `-live` in their names carry the cells of the browser lab. The four slide decks of day 3 of the multi-day format are assembled in `slides/` from the segments of `slides/_segments/day-3/`. Every slide deck starts from the two setup segments in `slides/_segments/shared/` and `slides/_segments/case/`: the shared one names no case study, and the setup chunk of the case study comes after it and gives the shared segments the addresses of the case study. The web slides have a folder of their own, because the `revealjs` key of `slides/_metadata.yml` would render the web slides twice, and `live/_metadata.yml` carries the same options under `live-revealjs`, with a style block that bounds the height of cell outputs. A slide deck is a list of `{{< include >}}` lines with its own agenda, aims and part dividers.

**How the optional runs are switched.** In the segment files, every slide of an optional run is marked with `.deepdive` and a `run` attribute (`tools`, `r`, `methods`, `multiverse`). A slide deck lists the runs that belong to its main flow under `core-runs:` in its YAML, and `slides/core-runs.lua` strips the `.deepdive` mark from those headings, so `nav-tools.html` neither hides them on the `d` key nor badges them as optional. A run that is not listed stays optional: it is hidden in lean mode and has the escape-hatch link on its first slide.

**Why no segment is included twice in one slide deck.** The segment files contain R chunks with labels, and knitr refuses a duplicate label, so each slide deck includes each segment at most once.

**Rebuilding a slide deck.** Edit the segment files for content, or the file of the slides for order and framing, and render the slides on their own (`quarto render live/short.qmd`). A change to a segment needs every slide deck that includes it rendered again (`grep -l "_x.qmd" live/*.qmd slides/*.qmd`). The project render fails at its final move step on this machine, so slide decks are rendered one at a time.

## Housing and racial bias {#housing-and-racial-bias}

The Housing case study is taught in the part-day format, in the full-day format, and in the multi-day format, whose second day is the full-day format. The part-day format runs in its slides alone, in two halves, with the browser lab as the fallback: nothing is installed, nothing is sent to the class chart and nothing is preregistered. The full-day format is worked in the workspace, with the slides showing each step and standing in, with the browser lab, when an installation fails. In Task 3 each participant chooses which of the analysts to reproduce; the four who recorded a statistic reproduce exactly from the public file, and P9W8Y, who recorded none, can be rerun but not matched. The [run sheet of the case study](guide.qmd) has the timings of the part-day, full-day and multi-day formats, the preparation that each format asks of participants, the expected numbers, the checks before the day and the order of what to cut.

## The self-taught format {#self-study}

The self-taught format takes the Housing case study in five stages, with the companion modules between the tasks, and ends on a project of each participant's own; a semester course can follow the same route in class. Its pages contain their own compression notes, written to the reader, because no facilitator is there to apply them, and each stage page gives the total of its stage and nothing finer. What the facilitator can still do for a self-study cohort is keep the live results pipeline running between deliveries, so that a result submitted alone appears on the Class results page of the case study ([`facilitator/live-results-setup.md`](https://github.com/CodeMoreh/ar4ds-eu/blob/main/facilitator/live-results-setup.md) in the repository of the site of the Europeanisation and the economy case study).

**The class chart.** The chart of the case study is on its Class results page, and it reads only the rows of this case study from the results Form shared by the case studies of the workshop. The labels of the Housing case study carry the word `housing` after the tag (`explore: [amber-otter-42] housing …`). The workspace keeps its tag in `.class-tag`, so ask a cohort to choose one nickname and to pass it as `nickname = "..."` every time. The chart keeps the rows of earlier deliveries until the sheet is cleared.
